messages:
Alice (Support): Hey team, opening thread for a customer escal (Acme Corp). They saw their org credits drop to 0 while ~15 long-running requests were still in-flight. Customer says they started a burst at 23:58 tenant local time, we returned 200s for a few calls, then at 00:00 they started seeing 429s and UI showed 0 credits. They also saw 'usage' still incrementing in billing UI for another ~4 minutes. Can billing/eng confirm whether inflight requests should be allowed to finish and whether the reset is tenant-local or strictly UTC?

Alice (Support): Repro steps the customer gave: 1) send 12 concurrent streaming requests between 23:58:10 and 23:59:50 2) observe some streams complete, then at 00:00:01 several streams fail with 429 3) billing shows their monthly credit balance became 0 at 00:00:00 and then usage shows spikes for a few minutes after. They provided an example curl they used:```bash
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \ -d '{"model":"redwood-x-large","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}'
```

Tom (Billing): Thanks Alice — looking at tenant 4321 billing logs now. Our current reset policy: monthly quota window is aligned to the tenant's billing timezone set on the org (not always UTC). For this tenant it's set to America/Los_Angeles, so their month rolled at 00:00 PDT. The balance transition in the ledger is recorded at 00:00:00 local. However, meter events are still emitted as tokens are consumed; I can see meter events with timestamps 00:00:02–00:03:10 that attached to the previous cycle and some that attached to the new cycle, looks like overlapping attribution.

Tom (Billing): Quick note — when balance hits zero we emit 429 for new requests. Historically we let inflight requests complete if they were accepted by the router before the decision point. We need to check if the router decision is based on a pre-check at enqueue time or re-checked at token generation.

JK (Eng): Copying logs. From the router trace for one of the failing streams:```
[router] recv req id=xyz at 23:59:59.800 local; quota_check passed (balance: 1200 tokens)
[serve] start stream id=xyz at 23:59:59.812
[tokenizer] emitted tokens until 00:00:01.120
[quota] post-gen check failed at 00:00:01.121 -> 429 returned
```
This implies we do an optimistic pre-check but also run a post-gen budget reconciliation which can cause an in-flight termination. That behavior was intentional to avoid negative balances, but it is surprising for customers who expect started streams to finish.

Sara (Oncall): @JK if we keep current behavior customers will see partial failures at boundary. Can we make a compatibility fix: allow streams that had a successful enqueue/quota pre-approval before the reset to be exempted until they finish (or until a small safety cap)? We should consider both security (avoid unlimited overrun) and UX.

JK (Eng): Idea: mark pre-approved requests with a transient reservation token that deducts a small safety buffer (e.g., 2k tokens) at enqueue time, guarantee finish up to reservation. If final count exceeds reservation we do a graceful termination with a clear error (and not mid-stream 429), or bill to next cycle if org policy allows. Implementation effort: router + quota service + accounting.

Tom (Billing): Policy question: do we allow billing to charge into next cycle automatically if an inflight request crosses month boundary? Currently we don't auto-charge next cycle unless there's a rollover/overage plan. For customers without rollover, requests should fail if no credits. But we can implement reservation to avoid mid-stream 429s.

QuotaBot: Automated note: tenant 4321 has billing timezone America/Los_Angeles, monthly reset day 1 at 00:00 local. Current ledger entry shows balance change at 2055014400 UTC (00:00 PDT).

Alice (Support): Customer prefers streams to finish if they were started before reset. They asked whether we can retroactively restore credits to let the specific failed requests complete. They also asked for guidance to avoid this: e.g., pre-purchase burst credits or set up rollover.

Tom (Billing): Short-term mitigation: we can manually credit tenant 4321 a small emergency buffer to cover the failed requests and refund later, but we should coordinate with legal/finance. Long-term: add reservation semantics or a pre-reserve option for orgs that run large streaming bursts around reset boundaries.

JK (Eng): I'll open an internal RFC for reserve-token workflow. For immediate patch, we can change router to prioritize pre-check timestamp (if enqueue_ts < reset_ts then allow completion up to a max cap). Quick patch risk: small window for abuse but low.

Sara (Oncall): For the customer's current incident, Alice — please send the list of request ids and timestamps. We'll do targeted crediting and a postmortem. Also add proactive communication to customers in months near DST change.

Alice (Support): Will do—thanks all. I'll ping legal/finance for the manual credit approval and follow up here once I have the IDs. :thumbsup:
